## Contributors
- 僧伽提婆 (A001589)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A three-fascicle Abhidharma summary attributed to "Venerable Mountain-Sage" ([尊者山賢](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B0%8A%E8%80%85%E5%B1%B1%E8%B3%A2) 尊者山賢, the calque-rendering of Vasubhadra / Sambhadra), retranslated by the Kashmirian master [Saṃghadeva](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9E%BF%E6%9B%87%E5%83%A7%E4%BC%BD%E6%8F%90%E5%A9%86) 瞿曇僧伽提婆 in the Eastern Jìn at Lúshān 廬山 in 391 CE under the patronage of [Huìyuǎn](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E9%81%A0) 慧遠. The work is the doublet companion of *[Sìāhánmù chāo jiě 四阿鋡暮抄解 (T1505)](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6a/KR6a0157)*, translated nine years earlier under [Dàoān](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E5%AE%89) at Yèsì from the same or a closely related Indic exemplar; the doublet relationship is acknowledged in the Taishō by 「No. 1506 [No. 1505]」 at the head of this text. The structure is the Tridharmaka triple-triad — three principal categories (Merit 德, Evil 惡, Basis-toward-awakening 依覺), each subdivided into three further triads, generating the title's "three measures."

**Abstract**

T1506 is the second and more discursive of the two Chinese translations of [Vasubhadra](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A9%86%E7%B4%A0%E8%B7%8B%E9%99%80)'s *Tridharmaka* abstract. [Saṃghadeva](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9E%BF%E6%9B%87%E5%83%A7%E4%BC%BD%E6%8F%90%E5%A9%86)'s retranslation was undertaken at Lúshān at the invitation of [Huìyuǎn](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E9%81%A0) precisely because the earlier Yèsì translation (T1505), prepared under heavy time-pressure during Dàoān's last years, was felt to be unsatisfactory; Huìyuǎn's preface to the new translation is candidly critical of the earlier rendering. T1506 thereby preserves a more polished version of the same Indic source. Modern scholarship (Frauwallner, Bart Dessein) treats the *Tridharmaka-śāstra* as a Bahuśrutīya / Saṃmitīya-school *abhidharma* composition, and the doublet as an unusually instructive case for evaluating early Chinese translation method: the same source rendered twice within a decade by two different teams under two different editorial regimes.

The internal structure is the *Tridharmaka* triple-triad (3 × 3 × 3): the three principal categories of *guṇa* (merit / 德), *doṣa* (evil / 惡), and *upādāya* (basis-toward-awakening / 依覺), each subdivided into three sub-triads; the third final triad (entry-into-liberation 解脫入: *saṃjñā* / *dhyāna* / 博聞 = "extensive hearing" / *sūtra-Abhidharma-Vinaya* triple recension of the canon) closes the text. The colophon at the end of fascicle three reads simply: 「依品第三真度說竟」.
